sanskrit: asminn arthāntare yuktam anarthaḥ pratipadyate yathāhaṃ vimṛśāmy ekas tat tāvac chrūyatāṃ mama
english: In this matter there lies another consideration where misfortune may result. As I alone reflect on it, let this be heard from me now.

sanskrit: saṃnyāsaṃ rocaye sādhu kāryasyāsya janārdana pratihanti mano me 'dya rājasūyo durāsadaḥ
english: I favour renunciation of this enterprise, O Janārdana. The Rājasūya sacrifice, so difficult to achieve, weighs heavily upon my mind today.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pārthaḥ prāpya dhanuḥśreṣṭham akṣayyau ca maheṣudhī rathaṃ dhvajaṃ sabhāṃ caiva yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Pārtha, having obtained the finest bow, two inexhaustible quivers, a chariot, a banner, and the assembly hall, then spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dhanur astraṃ śarā vīryaṃ pakṣo bhūmir yaśo balam prāptam etan mayā rājan duṣprāpaṃ yad abhīpsitam
english: O King, I have obtained this bow, weapons, arrows, prowess, allies, land, glory, and strength — all that was desired and hard to attain.

sanskrit: kule janma praśaṃsanti vaidyāḥ sādhu suniṣṭhitāḥ balena sadṛśaṃ nāsti vīryaṃ tu mama rocate
english: The learned who are well established rightly praise noble birth; yet there is nothing equal to strength, and prowess is what appeals to me.

sanskrit: kṛtavīryakule jāto nirvīryaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati kṣatriyaḥ sarvaśo rājan yasya vṛttiḥ parājaye
english: What will a kshatriya born in the lineage of Kṛtavīrya accomplish if he is without prowess, O King — one whose livelihood consists in defeat?

sanskrit: sarvair api guṇair hīno vīryavān hi tared ripūn sarvair api guṇair yukto nirvīryaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
english: Even one lacking all other qualities, if he possesses prowess, can overcome enemies; but what can one endowed with all qualities accomplish if he lacks prowess?

sanskrit: dravyabhūtā guṇāḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti hi parākrame jayasya hetuḥ siddhir hi karma daivaṃ ca saṃśritam
english: All qualities reside as substance in courage. Victory depends on accomplishment, and accomplishment in turn rests on action and fate.

sanskrit: saṃyukto hi balaiḥ kaś cit pramādān nopayujyate tena dvāreṇa śatrubhyaḥ kṣīyate sabalo ripuḥ
english: One who is endowed with forces but does not employ them through negligence — through that very negligence, the powerful enemy is weakened.

sanskrit: dainyaṃ yathābalavati tathā moho balānvite tāv ubhau nāśakau hetū rājñā tyājyau jayārthinā
english: Just as despondency is ruinous in the weak, so delusion is ruinous in the strong. Both these destructive causes must be abandoned by a king who seeks victory.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhavināśaṃ ca rājñāṃ ca parimokṣaṇam yadi kuryāma yajñārthaṃ kiṃ tataḥ paramaṃ bhavet
english: If we were to destroy Jarāsandha and free the imprisoned kings for the sake of the sacrifice, what greater achievement could there be?

sanskrit: anārambhe tu niyato bhaved aguṇaniścayaḥ guṇān niḥsaṃśayād rājan nairguṇyaṃ manyase katham
english: In non-undertaking, the certainty of failure is assured. When the qualities are beyond doubt, O King, how can you think there is a lack of merit?

sanskrit: kāṣāyaṃ sulabhaṃ paścān munīnāṃ śamam icchatām sāmrājyaṃ tu tavecchanto vayaṃ yotsyāmahe paraiḥ
english: The ochre robe is easily donned later by sages seeking tranquility; but desiring sovereignty for you, we shall fight the enemy.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca jātasya bhārate vaṃśe tathā kuntyāḥ sutasya ca yā vai yuktā matiḥ seyam arjunena pradarśitā
english: Vāsudeva said: Born in the lineage of Bharata and as the son of Kuntī, the fitting counsel has been shown by Arjuna.

sanskrit: na mṛtyoḥ samayaṃ vidma rātrau vā yadi vā divā na cāpi kaṃ cid amaram ayuddhenāpi śuśrumaḥ
english: We do not know the appointed time of death — whether by night or by day. Nor have we heard of anyone who is immortal even without fighting.

sanskrit: etāvad eva puruṣaiḥ kāryaṃ hṛdayatoṣaṇam nayena vidhidṛṣṭena yad upakramate parān
english: This much alone is what brings true satisfaction to men: to attack enemies by means of wise policy prescribed by scripture.

sanskrit: sunayasyānapāyasya saṃyuge paramaḥ kramaḥ saṃśayo jāyate sāmye sāmyaṃ ca na bhaved dvayoḥ
english: In battle, the highest course for sound and unfailing policy is this: when forces are equal, doubt arises; yet equality between the two parties is never truly so.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ nayam āsthāya śatrudehasamīpagāḥ katham antaṃ na gacchema vṛkṣasyeva nadīrayāḥ pararandhre parākrāntāḥ svarandhrāvaraṇe sthitāḥ
english: We, relying on good counsel and approaching near the enemy's person, how can we not bring him to his end — as rivers erode trees — attacking his weaknesses while guarding our own?

sanskrit: vyūḍhānīkair anubalair nopeyād balavattaram iti buddhimatāṃ nītis tan mamāpīha rocate
english: That one should not advance with arrayed but insufficient forces against a mightier foe — this is the policy of the wise, and I too approve of it here.

sanskrit: anavadyā hy asaṃbuddhāḥ praviṣṭāḥ śatrusadma tat śatrudeham upākramya taṃ kāmaṃ prāpnuyāmahe
english: Those who enter the enemy's abode undetected and blameless, attacking the enemy in person, shall accomplish that which they desire.

sanskrit: eko hy eva śriyaṃ nityaṃ bibharti puruṣarṣabha antarātmeva bhūtānāṃ tatkṣaye vai balakṣayaḥ
english: One man alone ever bears the fortune, O bull among men, as the inner self sustains all beings; when he is destroyed, the strength of the army is destroyed.

sanskrit: atha cet taṃ nihatyājau śeṣeṇābhisamāgatāḥ prāpnuyāma tataḥ svargaṃ jñātitrāṇaparāyaṇāḥ
english: And if, having slain him in battle, we proceed together with the remainder of the army, we shall attain heaven, devoted as we are to the protection of our kinsmen.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kṛṣṇa ko 'yaṃ jarāsaṃdhaḥ kiṃvīryaḥ kiṃparākramaḥ yas tvāṃ spṛṣṭvāgnisadṛśaṃ na dagdhaḥ śalabho yathā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Kṛṣṇa, who is this Jarāsandha? What is his valour, what his prowess — he who, having touched you who are like fire, was not burned like a moth?

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca śṛṇu rājañ jarāsaṃdho yadvīryo yatparākramaḥ yathā copekṣito 'smābhir bahuśaḥ kṛtavipriyaḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa said: Hear, O King, what valour and prowess Jarāsandha possesses, and why, though he repeatedly wronged us, he was left unchecked by us.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇīnāṃ tisṛṇām āsīt samaradarpitaḥ rājā bṛhadratho nāma magadhādhipatiḥ patiḥ
english: There was a king, proud in battle, named Bṛhadratha, lord among lords of Magadha, who commanded three akshauhinis of troops.

sanskrit: rūpavān vīryasaṃpannaḥ śrīmān atulavikramaḥ nityaṃ dīkṣākṛśatanuḥ śatakratur ivāparaḥ
english: He was handsome, endowed with prowess, glorious, of incomparable valour, his body always lean from ritual observances — like a second Indra of a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: tejasā sūryasadṛśaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ yamāntakasamaḥ kope śriyā vaiśravaṇopamaḥ
english: In splendour he was like the sun, in forbearance like the earth, in anger like Yama and Death together, in prosperity like Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit: tasyābhijanasaṃyuktair guṇair bharatasattama vyāpteyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā sūryasyeva gabhastibhiḥ
english: With his virtues combined with noble lineage, O best of the Bharatas, the entire earth was pervaded, as by the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: sa kāśirājasya sute yamaje bharatarṣabha upayeme mahāvīryo rūpadraviṇasaṃmate
english: That mighty hero, O bull of the Bharatas, married the two twin daughters of the king of Kāśi, who were equal in beauty and wealth.

sanskrit: tayoś cakāra samayaṃ mithaḥ sa puruṣarṣabhaḥ nātivartiṣya ity evaṃ patnībhyāṃ saṃnidhau tadā
english: That bull among men made a compact between them, saying, "I shall not transgress either of you," in the presence of both his wives.

sanskrit: sa tābhyāṃ śuśubhe rājā patnībhyāṃ manujādhipa priyābhyām anurūpābhyāṃ kareṇubhyām iva dvipaḥ
english: That king, O lord of men, shone magnificently between his two beloved, well-matched wives, like an elephant between two she-elephants.

sanskrit: tayor madhyagataś cāpi rarāja vasudhādhipaḥ gaṅgāyamunayor madhye mūrtimān iva sāgaraḥ
english: That lord of the earth, standing between the two of them, shone like the ocean in embodied form between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

sanskrit: viṣayeṣu nimagnasya tasya yauvanam atyagāt na ca vaṃśakaraḥ putras tasyājāyata kaś cana
english: His youth passed while he was immersed in the pleasures of the senses, yet no son was born to him to perpetuate his lineage.

sanskrit: maṅgalair bahubhir homaiḥ putrakāmābhir iṣṭibhiḥ nāsasāda nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ putraṃ kulavivardhanam
english: Through many auspicious fire-offerings and sacrifices desired by those longing for sons, that best of kings still did not obtain a son to further his family.

sanskrit: atha kākṣīvataḥ putraṃ gautamasya mahātmanaḥ śuśrāva tapasi śrāntam udāraṃ caṇḍakauśikam
english: Then he heard that Chandakaushika, the noble son of Kakṣīvat of the great-souled Gautama lineage, was exhausted from austerities nearby.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayāgataṃ taṃ tu vṛkṣamūlam upāśritam patnībhyāṃ sahito rājā sarvaratnair atoṣayat
english: The king, accompanied by his wives, gratified with all kinds of precious gifts that sage who had come by chance and was resting at the foot of a tree.

sanskrit: tam abravīt satyadhṛtiḥ satyavāg ṛṣisattamaḥ parituṣṭo 'smi te rājan varaṃ varaya suvrata
english: That best of sages, firm in truth and true in speech, said to him: "I am well pleased with you, O King. Choose a boon, O man of good vows."

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhāryaḥ praṇatas tam uvāca bṛhadrathaḥ putradarśananairāśyād bāṣpagadgadayā girā
english: Then Bṛhadratha, bowing with his wives, spoke to him in a voice choked with tears, despairing of ever seeing a son.

sanskrit: bṛhadratha uvāca bhagavan rājyam utsṛjya prasthitasya tapovanam kiṃ vareṇālpabhāgyasya kiṃ rājyenāprajasya me
english: Bṛhadratha said: O Blessed One, I who am of little fortune am setting out to the forest, abandoning my kingdom. What use is a boon to me? What use is a kingdom to one without a son?

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca etac chrutvā munir dhyānam agamat kṣubhitendriyaḥ tasyaiva cāmravṛkṣasya chāyāyāṃ samupāviśat
english: Kṛṣṇa said: Hearing this, the sage fell into deep meditation, his senses stirred, and he sat down in the shade of that very mango tree.

sanskrit: tasyopaviṣṭasya muner utsaṅge nipapāta ha avātam aśukādaṣṭam ekam āmraphalaṃ kila
english: As the sage sat there, there fell into his lap a single mango fruit, windfall-ripe and bitten by a parrot.

sanskrit: tat pragṛhya muniśreṣṭho hṛdayenābhimantrya ca rājñe dadāv apratimaṃ putrasaṃprāptikārakam
english: The best of sages took that fruit, consecrated it with his heart's power, and gave to the king that unequalled fruit which would bring the attainment of a son.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahāprājñas taṃ rājānaṃ mahāmuniḥ gaccha rājan kṛtārtho 'si nivarta manujādhipa
english: The great sage of vast wisdom said to the king: "Go, O King, your purpose is accomplished. Turn back, O lord of men."

sanskrit: yathāsamayam ājñāya tadā sa nṛpasattamaḥ dvābhyām ekaṃ phalaṃ prādāt patnībhyāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then that best of kings, understanding the instruction in accordance with the compact he had made, gave that one fruit to both his wives, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: te tad āmraṃ dvidhā kṛtvā bhakṣayām āsatuḥ śubhe bhāvitvād api cārthasya satyavākyāt tathā muneḥ
english: Those two auspicious queens cut that mango in two and ate it — both by reason of what was destined and also by the truth of the sage's word.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad garbhaḥ phalaprāśanasaṃbhavaḥ te ca dṛṣṭvā narapatiḥ parāṃ mudam avāpa ha
english: A pregnancy arose in each of them from eating the fruit, and the king, seeing this, was filled with the highest joy.

sanskrit: atha kāle mahāprājña yathāsamayam āgate prajāyetām ubhe rājañ śarīraśakale tadā
english: Then, O greatly wise one, when the time arrived, O King, both of them gave birth — each to a half of a body.

sanskrit: ekākṣibāhucaraṇe ardhodaramukhasphije dṛṣṭvā śarīraśakale pravepāte ubhe bhṛśam
english: Seeing those halves of a body — each with one eye, one arm, one leg, half an abdomen, half a face, half a hip — both women trembled greatly.

sanskrit: udvigne saha saṃmantrya te bhaginyau tadābale sajīve prāṇiśakale tatyajāte suduḥkhite
english: Those two anxious sisters consulted together, and in their great sorrow abandoned the still-living, breathing halves.

sanskrit: tayor dhātryau susaṃvīte kṛtvā te garbhasaṃplave nirgamyāntaḥpuradvārāt samutsṛjyāśu jagmatuḥ
english: The two nurses of those queens, having well wrapped those products of birth, went out through the inner palace gate and quickly cast them away.

sanskrit: te catuṣpathanikṣipte jarā nāmātha rākṣasī jagrāha manujavyāghra māṃsaśoṇitabhojanā
english: Those halves, cast at the crossroads, were then seized by a rakshasi named Jara, O tiger among men — one who feeds on flesh and blood.

sanskrit: kartukāmā sukhavahe śakale sā tu rākṣasī saṃghaṭṭayām āsa tadā vidhānabalacoditā
english: Intending to consume those easy-to-carry halves, that rakshasi joined them together, driven by the force of fate.

sanskrit: te samānītamātre tu śakale puruṣarṣabha ekamūrtikṛte vīraḥ kumāraḥ samapadyata
english: The moment those halves were brought together, O bull among men, and made into one form, a mighty boy came into being.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā rākṣasī rājan vismayotphullalocanā na śaśāka samudvoḍhuṃ vajrasāramayaṃ śiśum
english: Then that rakshasi, O King, her eyes wide with wonder, was unable to lift that infant whose very substance was like adamant.

sanskrit: bālas tāmratalaṃ muṣṭiṃ kṛtvā cāsye nidhāya saḥ prākrośad atisaṃrambhāt satoya iva toyadaḥ
english: The boy clenched his copper-hued fist, placed it in his mouth, and cried out with great fury like a rain-cloud full of water.

sanskrit: tena śabdena saṃbhrāntaḥ sahasāntaḥpure janaḥ nirjagāma naravyāghra rājñā saha paraṃtapa
english: At that sound the people of the inner palace were suddenly startled and rushed out, O tiger among men, together with the king, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: te cābale pariglāne payaḥpūrṇapayodhare nirāśe putralābhāya sahasaivābhyagacchatām
english: And those two exhausted women with their milk-filled breasts, who had despaired of obtaining a son, suddenly came forward as well.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā tathābhūte rājānaṃ ceṣṭasaṃtatim taṃ ca bālaṃ subalinaṃ cintayām āsa rākṣasī
english: Then seeing the king in that condition, his continued activity, and that very powerful boy, the rakshasi reflected.

sanskrit: nārhāmi viṣaye rājño vasantī putragṛddhinaḥ bālaṃ putram upādātuṃ meghalekheva bhāskaram
english: "Living within the domain of a king who yearns for a son, I ought not to take away this infant son, as a streak of cloud cannot cover the sun."

sanskrit: sā kṛtvā mānuṣaṃ rūpam uvāca manujādhipam bṛhadratha sutas te 'yaṃ maddattaḥ pratigṛhyatām
english: She assumed a human form and said to the lord of men: "O Bṛhadratha, this is your son — given by me. Please accept him."

sanskrit: tava patnīdvaye jāto dvijātivaraśāsanāt dhātrījanaparityakto mayāyaṃ parirakṣitaḥ
english: "Born of your two wives through the command of the best among the twice-born, abandoned by the nurses, he was protected by me."

sanskrit: tatas te bharataśreṣṭha kāśirājasute śubhe taṃ bālam abhipatyāśu prasnavair abhiṣiñcatām
english: Then, O best of Bharatas, those two auspicious daughters of the king of Kāśi quickly rushed to that boy and bathed him with streams of milk.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sarvaṃ tad upalabhya ca apṛcchan navahemābhāṃ rākṣasīṃ tām arākṣasīm
english: Then that king, filled with joy and having understood everything, questioned that rakshasi who appeared like fresh gold and unlike a rakshasi at all.

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ kamalagarbhābhe mama putrapradāyinī kāmayā brūhi kalyāṇi devatā pratibhāsi me
english: "Who are you, O one radiant as the heart of a lotus, who has given me a son? Speak freely, O auspicious one — you appear to me as a goddess."

sanskrit: rākṣasy uvāca jarā nāmāsmi bhadraṃ te rākṣasī kāmarūpiṇī tava veśmani rājendra pūjitā nyavasaṃ sukham
english: The rakshasi said: I am a rakshasi named Jara, O blessings to you, one who assumes forms at will. I dwelt happily in your household, O king of kings, being honoured there.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ pratyupakārārthaṃ cintayanty aniśaṃ nṛpa taveme putraśakale dṛṣṭavaty asmi dhārmika
english: Always thinking of how to return your kindness, O King, I, ever meditating on it, found these two half-portions of your son, O righteous one.

sanskrit: saṃśleṣite mayā daivāt kumāraḥ samapadyata tava bhāgyair mahārāja hetumātram ahaṃ tv iha
english: When joined by me, by the will of fate a boy came into being. It is by your own fortune, O great king; I was merely the instrument here.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca evam uktvā tu sā rājaṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata sa gṛhya ca kumāraṃ taṃ prāviśat svagṛhaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa said: Having spoken thus, O King, she vanished on the spot. The king, taking that boy, entered his own home.

sanskrit: tasya bālasya yat kṛtyaṃ tac cakāra nṛpas tadā ājñāpayac ca rākṣasyā māgadheṣu mahotsavam
english: The king performed all the rites proper for that child, and in honour of the rakshasi he ordered a great festival throughout Magadha.

sanskrit: tasya nāmākarot tatra prajāpatisamaḥ pitā jarayā saṃdhito yasmāj jarāsaṃdhas tato 'bhavat
english: His father, equal to Prajāpati, there performed the naming ceremony for him. Because he had been joined together by Jara, he thus became known as Jarāsandha — "joined by Jara."

sanskrit: so 'vardhata mahātejā magadhādhipateḥ sutaḥ pramāṇabalasaṃpanno hutāhutir ivānalaḥ
english: That son of the lord of Magadha, of great splendour, grew up, endowed with perfect strength, like a fire fed with oblations.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya punar eva mahātapāḥ magadhān upacakrāma bhagavāṃś caṇḍakauśikaḥ
english: Then after some time, the blessed Chandakaushika, the great ascetic, again came to Magadha.

sanskrit: tasyāgamanasaṃhṛṣṭaḥ sāmātyaḥ sapuraḥsaraḥ sabhāryaḥ saha putreṇa nirjagāma bṛhadrathaḥ
english: Delighted at his arrival, Bṛhadratha went out with his ministers, his retinue, his wives, and his son.

sanskrit: pādyārghyācamanīyais tam arcayām āsa bhārata sa nṛpo rājyasahitaṃ putraṃ cāsmai nyavedayat
english: That king honoured him with water for the feet, the guest-offering, and water for sipping, O Bharata, and presented his son along with the kingdom to the sage.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāṃ pārthivād bhagavān ṛṣiḥ uvāca māgadhaṃ rājan prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
english: The blessed sage, having accepted that honour from the king, spoke to the Magadha king with a soul rejoicing within.

sanskrit: sarvam etan mayā rājan vijñātaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā putras tu śṛṇu rājendra yādṛśo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "O King, all of this has been known to me through the eye of wisdom. But hear, O king of kings, what this son of yours shall become."

sanskrit: asya vīryavato vīryaṃ nānuyāsyanti pārthivāḥ devair api visṛṣṭāni śastrāṇy asya mahīpate na rujaṃ janayiṣyanti girer iva nadīrayāḥ
english: "The prowess of this mighty one shall not be matched by kings. Even weapons hurled by gods, O lord of the earth, shall not wound him — like rivers against a mountain."

sanskrit: sarvamūrdhābhiṣiktānām eṣa mūrdhni jvaliṣyati sarveṣāṃ niṣprabhakaro jyotiṣām iva bhāskaraḥ
english: "He shall blaze at the crown of all consecrated kings, dimming the splendour of them all, as the sun dims all other luminaries."

sanskrit: enam āsādya rājānaḥ samṛddhabalavāhanāḥ vināśam upayāsyanti śalabhā iva pāvakam
english: "Kings with prosperous forces and armies, encountering him, shall come to destruction — like moths meeting fire."

sanskrit: eṣa śriyaṃ samuditāṃ sarvarājñāṃ grahīṣyati varṣāsv ivoddhatajalā nadīr nadanadīpatiḥ
english: "He shall seize the accumulated glory of all kings, as in the rainy season the ocean — lord of rivers — swallows the high-watered rivers."
